_prompt:
You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: Two concurrent redemptions of the same token can both succeed, because the check and the write aren't under one lock.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Single-use is not atomic. `shop/auth.py` does `if token in _USED: raise` and then `_USED.add(token)` as separate steps. Probe: swap `_USED` for a set subclass whose `__contains__` sleeps 10 ms, then start 4 threads redeeming one token at `now=1`. Result: `['ada', 'ada', 'ada', 'ada']`, so four successful redeems and zero TokenUsed. Fix direction: a single lock around check-and-mark, or a `set.add` return value check.
- [minor] NaN or inf `now` makes a token never expire. Reproduced: `issue(now=float('nan'))` then `redeem(now=1e12)` returns 'ada'. Not in the criteria.
- [minor] An unhashable token (`['x']`) raises a bare `TypeError`, not `InvalidToken`. Reproduced. The criteria only list "", None, and never-issued strings.
- [minor] A non-numeric `now` (`'1'`) raises `TypeError` with no validation. Reproduced. Not in the criteria.
- [minor] `_TOKENS` and `_USED` grow without bound; there is no eviction of expired entries.
- [minor] The test file does not cover a falsy username (`""`/`None`) round-trip or NaN, though the code handles both (`issue('')` and `issue(None)` both round-trip in probes).
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) ===
GOAL: Make redeem_reset_token's single-use guarantee hold under concurrent redeems of the same token.
FILES: /tmp/ff-eval-aqw1zz54/workspace/shop/auth.py — redeem_reset_token currently does `if token in _USED: raise TokenUsed` ... `_USED.add(token)` as separate steps. A reviewer reproduced 4 threads all redeeming one token successfully by forcing interleaving between the check and the add.
CONSTRAINTS: Minimal change: add a module-level `threading.Lock()` and hold it around the lookup/used-check/expiry-check/mark section of redeem_reset_token (compute the default `now` before taking it is fine). Standard library only. Do not change any other behavior or error messages. No new tests required (races aren't deterministic to test); existing tests must keep passing. Touch only shop/auth.py.
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- issue_reset_token(username, now=None) and redeem_reset_token(token, now=None); now is Unix seconds (int or float); None means time.time(), checked with `is None` so now=0 is honored. Calls without now keep working (existing tests unchanged and passing).
- Successful redeem returns the username the token was issued for.
- A token redeemed more than 1800 s after issue raises TokenExpired. Exactly 1800 s after issue succeeds.
- Tokens are single-use: after one successful redeem, any further redeem raises TokenUsed — including when that later attempt is also past the expiry window; this holds under concurrent redeems of the same token.
- A failed redeem never marks a token used; redeeming an expired token twice raises TokenExpired both times.
- TokenExpired and TokenUsed are subclasses of InvalidToken; unknown tokens raise plain InvalidToken.
- ./check.sh passes; standard library only.
CHECKS: `cd /tmp/ff-eval-aqw1zz54/workspace && python3 -m unittest tests.test_auth -v`, then `./check.sh`.
